subject: Variance estimates with ds() versus dht2()

messages.author: 27dc2f77ea4fda39
messages.subject: Variance estimates with ds() versus dht2()
parts:
Hi again

I am conducting analysis on line transect data from a stratified study region (2 PAs), one species, two survey years. I require abundance estimates per region and per year (and I know there are some problems with regards to pooling multiple years).

I have found the model of my dreams for this species: it is a HR key function with PA as covariate. With this model I have produced abundance and density estimates per strata (the 4 possible year-pa combinations), but when I produce a summary() or print() of the ds object the variance are different compared to when I use dht2(). I think this may have something to do with the settings for "varn" of dht2 but when I try different options, there is still quite a big difference in CV and SE.

So my questions are:

1.) Why does this difference exists (how are the variances calculated differently between the ds() and dht2() functions?

2.) Which one to use?

3.) Or should I forget about this alltogether and give bootstrapping a go?

Thanks so much in advance!

Mylo

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Variance estimates with ds() versus dht2()
parts:
Mylo

There are lots of combinations governing variance estimation with the two functions in the package.  Recognise also that ds() is actually calling the function dht() for abundance estimation.  You've not specified where the differences in variances are manifested: at the stratum level or the global level.

The function dht2() is used when there is non-standard kinds of stratification and an overall estimate for the entire study area required different types of weighted averages.

I think in your situation (where you are not interested in study area-wide estimates, just the year/stratum-specific estimates), you can rely upon the computations carried out by ds() (via dht()).  Correct me if I'm wrong about my assumptions.

If you want some detail on the variance calculations used by dht2(), have a look at this diagram

https://examples.distancesampling.org/Distance-mult/strat.pdf

messages.author: 71f802310bdab6aa
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Variance estimates with ds() versus dht2()
parts:
Hi Eric

Many thanks for your quick response!

The differences are manifested both at the stratum and global level, although the difference in global level is much smaller (difference in CV is 0.02 for global versus 0.14-0.17 for stratum-level). Since the variance is much lower for dht2() compared to ds(), I’d prefer to use dht2(), and as the results are stratified, it does seem a correct approach.. However, I obviously don’t want to go for an increase in precision at the cost of accuracy. Given the added detail, do you still think ds() is better for this particular analysis? If so, can the proportions of variance contribution (df, encounter rate, cluster size), also be calculated using df?

I failed to mention that in addition to the stratum specific estimates (year/PA), I am also interested in obtaining a study-area wide estimate for each year (i.e. combined PA, singular year).

Following your cheat sheet, as well as your recommendations in this conversation: https://groups.google.com/g/distance-sampling/c/BAhQmzts9nI/m/cBA-2ndyAwAJ

I use the following code for stratum-specific estimates:

dht2(BAN_16_20_HR_PA_T79, flatfile=BAN_16_20, strat_formula= ~Region.Label, convert_units = conversion.factor,
                     er_est = c("O1"), multipliers = NULL,sample_fraction = 1, ci_width = 0.95, stratification="geographical")


(where region.label is either of the 4 year/PA combinations). My example is actually a hybrid between geographical and effort_sum stratification. I checked and effort_sum did produce the same stratum-level results (with the difference being in total versus average abundance estimate & variance for the pooled global estimate).

Then, for the combined PA per Year estimate, I take a ‘production line’ approach, by merging the Region.Label in to 2 categories and adjusting the total area (summed of 2 PAs). And then using the same code as above. I am not sure if this is an entirely correct approach? It does yield an abundance estimate that is roughly the sum of the above, but it does not account for the different area size or effort for both PAs (which is relatively minor: 1,670 versus 1,736 sq. km area, and 1.391 versus 1,368km effort).

I also tried strat_formula= ~YEAR, but that keeps coming with an error message:

>1 Area defined for a single stratum label, check data

 Would you have a recommendation on how to approach the combined PA/per year estimate?

I gave the bootdht function a go as well, but it only produces results for the global estimate. Perhaps I shouldn’t add even more options then we already have!

Thanks again so much for your advice!

Mylo

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Variance estimates with ds() versus dht2()
parts:
Mylo

dht() (called by ds()) handles geographic stratification just fine, so no particular need to use dht2() when stratification is present.  The untidy bit of your analysis is that as you note, you're defining strata using a combination of space and time.  I don't actually know what is correct in this situation.

dht() does not have the added code to produce the variance component calculation you request, but it is a pretty straightforward calculation that could be done manually (see below)

A possible partial explanation for your difference in CVs among your various analytical combinations is the use of the O1 option for encounter rate variance; I don't believe we've tested that option. What was your motivation for choosing that encounter rate variance calculation? It should be used when there are gradients in line length along with gradients in animal density; your ds() analysis cannot directly access the equivalent option  when calling dht().

Given the bespoke nature of your analysis, my suggestion for your region-wide annual estimates would be to use the "stratum" specific estimates from your 4 year/stratum estimates and their measures of precision; manually combine them in the manner shown in the cheat-sheet from yesterday for geographic stratification.  I appreciate it's not elegant, but we don't have code that handles your specific situation.

messages.author: 71f802310bdab6aa
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Variance estimates with ds() versus dht2()
parts:
Thanks again Eric

It sounds the dht() (called by ds()) is the tried and tested solution, so I’ll move ahead with that. In case anyone is interested in delving deeper in the dht2 variance mystery: I used all different possible varn options for line transects (R2,3,4, S1, and O1,02,03), and the variances produced were near-similar whilst all very different to that of dht(). I chose O1 as it is described as “systematic line placement, post-stratification with overlapping strata (akin to S1)”, and my data for different years overlaps in space.

Moving on and ahead: Following your solution on the region-wide estimate, summing all 4 year/stratum estimates would not give me the desirable 2PA for 1 year, but rather 2PA summed for both years. If I use the 2 year/stratum estimates within the desired year then following the geographic stratification would be easy (just summing), but would it not ignore the variance caused by using a pooled DF for 2 years? I wouldn’t want to use the effort-weighted sum either as it gives an average over the 2 years and 2 areas.

I promise that was my final variance question J thanks again!

Milou
